A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BOB research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original few-shot and long-tail classification experiments, component ablations, distribution comparisons, and training-duration analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds prompt-source comparisons, data-quantity sweeps, attribute ablations, and results from additional seeds.

M1.justification: The main two-stage BOB pipeline, architectures, and objectives remain unchanged. Section 7.4 adds evaluated procedural variants that sample background and pose independently or incorporate color as another attribute. These are limited adaptations tested through ablations, not replacements for the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Aircraft, Car, CUB, and Pets for few-shot classification and CUB-LT and Flower-LT for long-tail classification. The new sample-count sweeps and qualitative examples use retained datasets and tasks; ImageNet is not added as a downstream evaluation benchmark.

E2.justification: The seven main comparison methods remain unchanged. v2 Table 3 adds explicit prompt-source comparison variants using Diff-II's dataset-level suffixes and 100 GPT-generated background/pose descriptions. These are evaluated alternatives to BOB's extracted contexts, rather than newly added full benchmark baselines.

E3.justification: The main splits, backbones, generation settings, and training protocols are retained. New Aircraft experiments vary real images per class over 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16, and synthetic images over 100–500. The synthetic-data sweep reduces classifier epochs to 100, 50, 33, 25, and 20 to approximately hold gradient updates constant.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis with prompt-diversity controls, real- and synthetic-data scaling, joint versus independent context sampling, attribute composition, seed stability, and qualitative comparisons on Car, CUB, and Pets. Existing epoch, FID, and caption-model analyses remain. The class-level ablation with preservation moves into Table 3; its counterpart without preservation is omitted.

E5.justification: Unlike v1, v2 Section 7.5 explicitly reports three additional runs of five-shot Aircraft using different few-shot images, with individual seed results for BOB and DataDream in Table 8. This adds localized repeatability evidence, but no confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty summaries for the main benchmark tables.

E6.justification: All original per-dataset scores in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results for prompt sources, data scaling, attributes, and seeds. Examples include 72.10% for GPT-generated contexts versus 73.78% for BOB, and 61.09% with color versus 60.31% with background/pose. The 68.01% ablation entry disappears. Pets overlap reporting changes from 22/39 to 25/37 with revised mappings. New Table 1 averages include an error: MAE/Diff-II five-shot is printed as 72.69%, although its listed scores average 72.96%.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the causal graph and back-door adjustment formula but removes v1's explicit sample-ID definition, the independence argument P(I|Y) approximately equals P(I), and the written confounding path. This reduces the formal justification without adding a theorem or changing the retained adjustment identity.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain context preservation during fine-tuning and context marginalization during generation to improve synthetic training data. The abstract and introduction retain the headline Aircraft comparison and superiority in 18 of 24 settings. Added experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that prompt diversity matters but does not fully explain BOB's advantage. Its new limitations paragraph makes reliable class-agnostic attributes an explicit applicability condition and identifies automatic attribute discovery and coarse-grained ImageNet recognition as challenges. These refine the existing mechanism and scope rather than replace them.

D1.justification: The existing hyperparameter and generation tables and validation-set instructions are retained. v2 documents settings for its new sweeps, including epoch adjustments, but removes v1's explicit code-availability statement and repository link. This is a change in access documentation; the PDFs do not establish that the code itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liu et al.'s work on feasibility of synthetic training data and removes Pearl's Causality reference. Related-work positioning shifts emphasis from integrating diverse captions across stages toward preserving controllability and marginalizing spurious associations. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose are retained. v2 rewrites the context-marginalization explanation, expands the five-shot versus ten-shot discussion, edits wording and author information, and reorganizes Appendices A/B into supplementary Sections 6/7. These are localized narrative revisions alongside the new scientific material.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the main paper from one column to two, adds an opening comparison figure, and adds several supplementary plots and image grids. It combines the FID and caption-model plots, converts the epoch table into a plot, adds average columns to Table 1, and restructures the component-ablation display.

improvement.justification: The new prompt controls, controlled data-quantity sweeps, attribute tests, and three additional seeds strengthen understanding and robustness evidence beyond v1's existing evaluations. Explicit applicability limitations also improve qualification of the claims. The gain is limited because most new quantitative analysis concerns Aircraft and the main benchmark results are unchanged. Removal of the code link and the erroneous new Table 1 average partly offset these benefits.
